claim_summary: GenAutoML contributes LLM-driven time-series architecture synthesis, traceback-guided shape repair, live runtime integration, and temporal normalization and preprocessing safeguards for forecasting and anomaly detection.

claim_evidence.quote: By feeding back the traceback and dimension mismatch errors to the LLM used to generate them, the Sandboxed Reflection Loop iterates through the process to help debug the architecture in preparation for final deployment [8].
To address this, we integrate a Dynamic Reversible Instance Normalization (Dyn-RevIN) wrapper, directly adopting the mathematical framework proposed by [19].

modules.name: Task-specific architecture synthesis and search
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK: the procedure generates candidate architectures for defined forecast/reconstruction objectives and evaluates them by task losses; changing task objectives changes the architectures and optimization criteria. Counterfactual: the synthesis objective and training/search setup must change across forecasting and anomaly detection, so not generic temporal handling (GTS) or task-neutral runtime (GH).
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - task-specific architecture synthesis and optimization

evidence.quote: By using the automated architectural synthesis, the agent writes class definitions directly to a dynamic registry, enabling the system to "invent" complex structures like multi-scale Inception blocks [31] or residual dilated convolutions based on the user’s textual description of the data [13].

Finally, through Dynamic Discovery, by treating these hallucinated models as first-class citizens, the optimization loop is able to compare baselines (like DLinear) [45] and agent-generated models (like ResNetBlockModel) [13] under the same mathematical circumstances.

modules.name: Sandboxed shape validation and traceback repair
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK: validation asserts the required forecast horizon output shape and repairs violations against this task-specific contract. Counterfactual: the output horizon and verifier must be redesigned for another task; it is not generic GTS temporal evidence validation or task-neutral GH error recovery.

evidence.quote: The system programmatically asserts that the output shape strictly conforms to the expected horizon dimensions RB×H×D .

Because of this , even if the forward pass fails or returns an invalid shape, the framework can capture the execution traceback and dimension mismatch errors and then feeding them back to the LLM as an additional prompt.

modules.name: Runtime architecture discovery and hot-swapping
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK no: registry discovery and code hot-swapping do not embody a task output criterion. R3_2 GTS no: class loading and module-cache updates need no temporal semantics. R3_3 GH yes: this is task-neutral runtime execution and integration.

evidence.quote: First, through Introspection, the system searches the dynamic registry for new class definitions that inherit from torch.nn.Module using Python’s inspect module. Next, Hot-Swapping updates the module cache in real-time by using importlib.reload.

This eliminates the need for a system reboot by enabling the system to instantiate new architectures and register them as legitimate candidates in the Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization search space.

modules.name: Dynamic RevIN statistical wrapper
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK no: the wrapper does not define a task objective; R3_2 GTS yes: it computes and reverses per-instance statistics across temporal input windows to stabilize numerical series, independent of a single task; R3_3 GH is therefore not reached.

evidence.quote: To address this, we integrate a Dynamic Reversible Instance Normalization (Dyn-RevIN) wrapper, directly adopting the mathematical framework proposed by [19].

This wrapping mechanism ensures that even if the AI-generated architecture is poorly scaled, the Dyn-RevIN layer enforces a stationary learning environment, which we demonstrate is essential for stable convergence.

modules.name: Causal resampling and missing-value preprocessing
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK no: resampling and causal imputation do not embed one task's output criterion; R3_2 GTS yes: they explicitly depend on sampling frequency, timestamps, and information availability to prevent look-ahead leakage; R3_3 GH is not reached.
rubric_path: R3_2_GTS:yes - frequency, chronology and availability-aware temporal processing

evidence.quote: As a result, GenAutoML uses asymmetric regularization when resampling a temporal series to ensure that the data is sampled at a consistent overall frequency without introducing look-ahead bias.

To ensure optimal data retention, all null values in the training set are resolved using a bilateral interpolation (limit_direction=’both’). Conversely, the test and validation sets only utilize causal forward-filling (limit_direction=’forward’).

temporal_validity.quote: We maintain our rigorous causal chronological split of 70% for Training, 10% for Validation, and 20% for Testing to prevent temporal data leakage across all datasets.
